normalization_or_editorial_flags.issue: Partial diacritization is inconsistent; normalize display policy across the workbook.
Normalize terminal punctuation to the chosen Arabic/English learner style; current rows mix periods and Arabic question punctuation inconsistently.
ألي بهذه البرتقالة؟ is formal/elliptical and should receive a native-editorial naturalness review for modern MSA.
كريم لأشعة الشمس is awkward for sunscreen; prefer a standard learner term such as واقٍ من الشمس / واقي شمس after native-register review.
كم تفاحة؟ is elliptical for 'How many apples are there?'; acceptable in context but consider a complete standalone learner sentence.
Normalize أنى/أنّى orthography and remove stray space before punctuation; the expression is more literary than the rest of the beginner bank.
Degree expressions are inconsistent (كثيرًا / لهذه الدرجة); review naturalness and MSA register, especially منحوس which is colloquial in many contexts.
Arabic specifies 'my call' while English says 'answer me'; tighten bilingual equivalence.
Hold on maps to انتظر in context, but the learner pair should be checked for register and request politeness.
Arabic wording means roughly 'Please, what time is it?' whereas English says 'Excuse me'; rank 403 already supplies عفوًا. Review duplication/equivalence.
Case marking after أن is omitted/inconsistent in this partially vocalized corpus; normalize rather than mixing fully and partially marked forms.
Arabic explicitly includes عادةً while English asks general frequency; not contradictory, but standalone equivalence can be tightened.
Arabic explicitly adds في المستقبل ('in the future'); English omits it. Semantically compatible, but the pair is not exact.
English includes degree 'so tired'; Arabic only says 'tired'. Consider جدًا / إلى هذا الحد if exact alignment is desired.
بالداخل is understandable but less idiomatic than الدخول/إلى الداخل for modern MSA; rank 476 is cleaner.
